High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Applicant :- Moola And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Deepak Kumar Pal

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Deepak Kumar Pal, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Kunwar Tejendra
Bahadur, learned Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicants on bail in Case Crime No.
129 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 306, 504 IPC, Police Station Mandawar, District Bijnor, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the co-accused Vipin i.e. husband of the deceased under section 498A, 304B, 504 and 3/4 D.P. Act and according to the FIR, marriage of the deceased was performed with co-accused Vipin on 3.3.2019 and after marriage he tortured his wife for want of dowry and on 23.4.2023 he committed the murder of the deceased by administering some poisonous substance.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicants are in-laws of the deceased and they were not named in the FIR but during investigation

, on the basis of statement of the brother of the Moola And Another vs State Of U.P. on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137565809/
1 deceased, they were made accused in the present matter.

entities.text: Moola And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submitted that during investigation, dying declaration of the deceased was procured by the Investigating Officer and after dying declaration of the deceased, case was converted under section 306 IPC.
5.

He further submitted that only being parents of the husband of the deceased, applicants also made accused in the present matter and deceased in her dying declaration dated 23.4.2023 did not make any allegation against the applicant and categorically stated that there was no dispute with anyone.
He further submitted that therefore, considering the dying declaration of the deceased applicants may be enlarged on bail.
6. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the arguments on fact advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Applicants are in-laws of the deceased and they were not named in the FIR and it appears that during investigation after recorded the statement of the brother of the deceased applicants also made accused in the present matter.

9. From the perusal of the record, it further reflects that dying declaration of the deceased was recorded by doctor on 23.4.2023 and in the dying declaration also deceased did not make any allegation against anyone including her in-laws i.e. applicants.
10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, particularly the dying declaration of the deceased, in my view, applicants are entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicants-Moola and Kusum, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless their personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade their from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicants shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

2 13.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicants.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
